The petitioner/ State has sought leave to appeal against the judgment dated 27-9-2021 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge (FTC)-CUM-Special Judge (under POCSO Act, 2012) in Spl.
Cri. Case (Under POCSO Act) No. 31/2021 whereby the respondent/accused has been acquitted of the charge punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code read with Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (in short ' POCSO Act' )and Section 3(2)(va)
of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act (in short, ('SCST Act' ).
2. Case of the prosecution, in brief, father of the prosecutrix lodged written complaint (Ex.P-3) on the basis of which FIR (Ex.P-4) was registered, to the effect that he belonged to Ghasia caste and is member of scheduled caste.

sentences.text: On 13.06.2019 he along with prosecutrix and other family members had gone to attend a marriage party in the nearby relation to the house of one Laxmi Prasad.
In the evening hours he along with his family, except the prosecutrix, returned back.
During late evening by 9 PM when the prosecutrix did not return back home, he enquired about her at the marriage place, but could not find her whereabouts.
On 14.06.2019, in the morning at around 10-11 AM one of his relative brother namely, Rajbahadur informed that the accused while inducing the prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage had kidnapped her.
On the same night at around 10 PM prosecutrix was found, on the way to Patna.

sentences.text: She had also disclosed that on the next morning on 14th June, 2019 the accused brought her to Ibrahim Khan's house at village : Sammapara /Patna and in the night escaped while dropping her on the road.
Based on such report, FIR was registered under section 363, 366, 376(2)(i)IPC r/w section 4, 6 of the POCSO Act and section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act.

After statement of prosecutrix,
the accused was arrested.
Prosecutrix and accused were got medically examined with consent.

After investigation, charge-sheet was filed before the court of Special Judge under the SCST Act and charges were framed u/s 363, 366, 376(3) IPC r/w section 4(2) of the POCSO Act and sections 3(2)(v) & 3(2)(va) of the SC/ST Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
3. To bring home charges, prosecution has examined 14 witnesses.
Statement of accused was recorded under section 313 CrPC wherein he denied the circumstances appearing against him and has pleaded false implication.

4. Learned trial Court after appreciating the evidence available on record, recorded finding that on the date of incident i.e. on 13-6-2019, the prosecutrix was not child within the meaning of Section 2(d) of the POCSO Act, the also that the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt with regard to other offence for which the respondent was charged and acquitted him of all the offences.

5. Mr. Gagan Tiwari, learned counsel for the State submitted though the scope of interference with the order of acquittal is very much limited but on the other hand the appellate Court is vested with wide powers of re-appreciation of the evidence in the matter.

It is submitted that it is the settled position of law that, if reappraisal of the evidence goes to show that the finding of acquittal recorded by the Trial Court is unjust and perverse then the appellate court is empowered to set-aside the same and reverse the order of acquittal and convict the accused appropriately.

It is also submitted that, the learned Trial Court committed error in disbelieving the case of prosecution merely for the reason that the witnesses have turned hostile to some extent during their examination.
It is also submitted that in her statement before Magistrate u/s 164 Cr.P.C. prosecutrix had categorically narrated the incident and duly supported the case of the prosecution.

It is argued that learned trial Court failed to consider Section 311 of Cr.P.C. in not examining the witnesses in proper perspective manner to reveal the truth when most of them were turning hostile without any reason from their earlier statements.

It is also submitted that the Court below failed to appreciate that the burden of proof as per Section 29 of the POCSO Act is on the accused when prima-facie the prosecutrix have deposed against accused in her statement under Section 164 of CrPC.

The learned Court below failed to appreciate that there is no allegations of malafide against the prosecution by any witnesses on the contrary have admitted the investigation which has been carried out on the complaint made.
In the statement of victim before the court below, she also clearly stated that she was subjected to act of rape by accused.
This statement of commission of alleged act has remained uncontroverted in the cross- examination; hence, the case of the prosecution was proved by the prosecutrix.
It is submitted that all the elements of the offences for which accused was charged are present in the prosecution case ex-facie, even then the accused has been acquitted.
Therefore, instant CRMP may be allowed and the acquittal appeal may be registered.

sentences.text: We have heard Mr. Gagan Tiwari, learned Deputy Government Advocate appearing for petitioner/State and gone through the records of the trial Court.

7. Prosecutrix ( P.W.1 ) has stated in her statement that in the night when she came out of her house to throw waste part of vegetables, accused reached there, gagged her and dragged to a bore well room situated at village Ranai and subjected her to forcible sexual intercourse 2-3 times.
She was threatened by him to kill if she raised alarm.
In the next morning accused took her to his father's quarter on foot.

On the next day, at around 4 pm she was sent for medical examination, thereafter,
as per Dr. Priyanka Pandey (P.W. 13), who examined the prosecutrix, has stated that there was no external injury on body of prosecutrix and also there was no sign of recent sexual intercourse with her.

Learned trial Court has considered the material contradictions in the statement of prosecutrix (P.W. 1) and considering entire material on record, has acquitted the accused from all the charges.
8.

The Supreme Court in the case of Babu Vs. State of Kerala, [(2010) 9 SCC 189] has laid down the principle to be followed in appeal against the acquittal under Section 378 of the Cr.P.C. and it has been held that Appellate Court should not ordinarily set aside acquittal in a case where two views are possible, though the views of Appellate Court may be the more probable one and held in para 12 as under:-
" 12.

entities.text: Babu Vs. State of Kerala, [(2010) 9 SCC 189]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court time and again has laid down the guidelines for the High Court to interfere with the judgment and order of acquittal passed by the trial court.
The appellate court should not ordinarily set aside a judgment of acquittal in a case where two views are possible, though the view of the appellate court may be the more probable one.

While dealing with a judgment of acquittal, the appellate court has to consider the entire evidence on record, so as to arrive at a finding as to whether the views of trial court were perverse or otherwise unsustainable.

The appellate court is entitled to consider whether in arriving at a finding of fact, the trial court had failed to take into consideration admissible evidence and/or had taken into consideration the evidence brought on record contrary to law.

Similarly, wrong placing of burden of proof may also be a subject matter of scrutiny by the appellate court."
9.

Thereafter, in Anwar Ali & Another Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh [(2020) 10 SCC 166] Supreme Court has reviewed its earlier decisions including Babu (supra) reiterating the principles laid down therein.

entities.text: Anwar Ali & Another Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh [(2020) 10 SCC 166]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Having considered the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner and in view of the law on the appeal against acquittal and the scope and ambit of Section 378 Cr.P.C., we are of the considered opinion that trial Court has rightly acquitted the accused from all the charges and it findings are is based on evidence available on record.

Thus, we do not find any compelling &
substantial reasons to interfere with the judgment of acquittal recorded by the trial Court.
11. Accordingly, CRMP, application seeking leave to appeal is rejected and the appeal is also dismissed.
